chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Yahya ibn 'Imran al-Halabi from Abd al-Hamid al-Ta'i said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'We are pedestrians, so what should we do?' He said, 'As for the people of carriages, they used to pray al-Ghadah (the morning prayer) in Mina, but as for you, proceed and pray wherever you are on the road.'
And when he proceeds to 'Arafat, he should supplicate with the supplication that was narrated:

key_terms.الْغَدَاةَ: The morning prayer (Fajr) offered during Hajj rituals
key_terms.بِمِنًى: In Mina, a location near Mecca central to Hajj rituals
key_terms.عَرَفَاتٍ: 'Arafat, the plain where the standing (wuquf) of Hajj takes place

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for pedestrians regarding the morning prayer during Hajj compared to those on carriages?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the flexibility (*rukhsah*) granted to pilgrims based on their mode of travel, distinguishing between those with mounts who remain in Mina and those on foot who pray en route. It highlights the practical jurisprudence of the Imams, emphasizing ease for the weak or distant pilgrim, while linking the journey to 'Arafat with the recitation of a specific, previously narrated supplication, underscoring the spiritual gravity of the approach to the Station of Mercy.
